dervis-irab:15-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَهْجَعُونَ) Hujūʿ is escaping from sleep, that is, sleeping little. In al-Mukhtār: "Hujūʿ is sleeping at night (its verb pattern is khaḍaʿa); a hajʿa is a light sleep, and one says: 'I came to so-and-so after a hajʿa,' that is, after a light sleep in the night." The poet said:
قد حصت البيضة رأسي فما ... أطعم نوما غير تهجاع
أسعى على جل بني مالك ... وكل امرئ في شأنه ساع
(The helmet has shorn my head, so I taste no sleep but a light dozing; I strive on behalf of the greater part of Banū Mālik, and every man strives in his own affair.) The verses are by Qays al-Aslat. Ḥaṣṣat means "destroyed" or "shaved"; al-bayḍa is the helmet worn on the head in war, that is, it shaved the hair of my head through my wearing it constantly in war. Sleep is likened to food by way of istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor).

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ) inna and its noun; and فِي جَنَّاتٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, which is its khabar (predicate); وَعُيُونٍ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جَنَّاتٍ. (آخِذِينَ ما آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَبْلَ ذلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ)
آخِذِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the khabar of inna, that is, "they abide, content with what He has given them, delighted in it". مَا is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of آخِذِينَ; and the clause آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ is its ṣila (relative clause). inna and its noun, and the clause كانُوا is its khabar; the sentence is a justification of what was mentioned. قَبْلَ ذلِكَ is an adverbial attached to مُحْسِنِينَ, and مُحْسِنِينَ is the khabar of كانُوا. (كانُوا قَلِيلًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ما يَهْجَعُونَ) The clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) with no grammatical position, because it is an explanation of their doing good. kāna and its noun; قَلِيلًا is an adverb of time attached to يَهْجَعُونَ, or an adjective of an omitted absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), that is, "a little sleep"; مِنَ اللَّيْلِ is an adjective of قَلِيلًا; and مَا is redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the fewness. For that reason He described them as spending the night in prayer (mutahajjidīn). They also permitted that مَا be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), in the position of the nominative as the agent of قَلِيلًا, that is, "their sleeping was little"; this is an easy and good construction. It may also be a relative (mawṣūla) meaning "that which", with the returning pronoun omitted, its implied form being: "they were little of the night, of the time in which they sleep"; there is strain in this. Some rejected that مَا be maṣdariyya, because قَلِيلًا would then apply to the sleeping, since it is its agent, and the phrase مِنَ اللَّيْلِ cannot be an adjective of the "little" nor an explanation of it, and cannot belong to the ṣila of the maṣdar because it precedes it; this is not so if it is relative, for then قَلِيلًا applies to the night, as if He had said "little is the measure in which they sleep of the night", so nothing prevents مِنَ اللَّيْلِ from being an explanation of the "little" on this reading. The text of Abū l-Baqāʾ's statement: "His saying, the Exalted, «كانوا قليلا»: there are two views regarding the khabar of kāna. The first is ما يهجعون, and in مَا on this view there are two possibilities: one, that it is redundant, that is, 'they slept little', with قليلا an adjective of an adverb or a maṣdar, that is, 'a little time' or 'a little sleep'; and the second, that it is negative, as some grammarians mentioned, but this was rejected, because what lies within the scope of a negative cannot precede it, and قليلا is within its scope. The second view is that قليلا is the khabar of kāna and مَا is maṣdariyya, that is, 'their sleeping was little', as you say 'their sleeping was scant'; on this view it is also permissible that ما يهجعون be a badal of the noun of kāna, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and مِنَ اللَّيْلِ may not be attached to يهجعون on this view, since that would put the object of a maṣdar ahead of it; rather it is accusative as an explanation (tabyīn), that is, attached to an omitted verb which يهجعون explains. Some said the sentence is complete at قليلا, then He began anew, saying: مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ما يهجعون. This is remote, for if you make مَا negative, it is invalid for the reason we mentioned, and if you make it maṣdariyya there is no praise in it, since all people sleep at night." (وَبِالْأَسْحارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; بِالْأَسْحارِ is attached to يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ, and the bāʾ means "in"; هُمْ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ is the khabar; what is attached to the khabar was put first because it is permissible to put the operator ahead. (وَفِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ) The wāw is a conjunction; فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ is a fronted khabar and حَقٌّ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; لِلسَّائِلِ is attached to an omitted element, an adjective; وَالْمَحْرُومِ is conjoined to السَّائِلِ; and the sentence is conjoined to the khabar of kāna, so it is a third khabar. (وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آياتٌ لِلْمُوقِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; فِي الْأَرْضِ is a fronted khabar, آياتٌ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and لِلْمُوقِنِينَ an adjective of آياتٌ. (وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ is a khabar whose mubtadaʾ is omitted because what precedes it indicates it, the implied form being "آيات"; the hamza is for rebuking interrogation (istifhām inkārī); the fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied omitted element; لا is negative, and تُبْصِرُونَ is a nominative imperfect verb. (وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَما تُوعَدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; فِي السَّماءِ is a fronted khabar and رِزْقُكُمْ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is a conjunction, and مَا is a relative noun conjoined to رِزْقُكُمْ; تُوعَدُونَ is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is a ṣila whose returning pronoun is omitted. (فَوَ رَبِّ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِثْلَ ما أَنَّكُمْ تَنْطِقُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; رَبِّ السَّماءِ is genitive by the wāw, and الْأَرْضِ is conjoined to السَّماءِ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear). inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and حَقٌّ is its khabar. مِثْلَ, with the accusative, is an adjective of an omitted absolute object, that is, "it is the truth, a truth like your speaking"; it may also be accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in لَحَقٌّ, and it was said to be a ḥāl from لَحَقٌّ even though it is indefinite; al-Jarmī and Sībawayh allowed that in several places in his book. Speech (nuṭq) here denotes speaking with letters and sounds in an ordering of meanings; and people say: "This is true as surely as you are here" and "This is true as surely as you see and hear." And مَا is redundant, as al-Khalīl stated explicitly; it was also said to be an indefinite noun with a descriptive clause, in the position of the genitive by annexation to مِثْلَ. It was also said that when he annexed a verb to an indeclinable word, namely his saying أَنَّكُمْ, he made it indeclinable, as he made it indeclinable in يَوْمَئِذٍ in such cases as مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ, and as in "عَلى حينَ عاتَبْتُ الْمَشيبَ عَلى الصِّبا", and in the verse mentioned earlier:
لم يمنع الشرب منها غير أن نطقت ... حمامة في غصون ذات أرقال
(Nothing kept it from drinking from it except that a dove cooed among branches that swayed.) Here غير is in the position of the nominative as the agent of يمنع. These vague nouns, such as مثل, يوم, حين and غير, become indeclinable when annexed to an indeclinable word, because they take on its indeclinability: the muḍāf takes from the muḍāf ilayhi what it has of definiteness and indefiniteness, of conditionality and interrogation. You say "this is the servant of Zayd" and "the companion of the judge", and the noun becomes definite by annexation to a definite; and you say "the servant of whom he strikes" and it is interrogative; and you say "the companion of whom he strikes I strike" and it is conditional. It was also read with the nominative, as an adjective of حَقٌّ. inna and its noun, and the clause تَنْطِقُونَ is its khabar, and its clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. And if you make مَا an indefinite noun with a descriptive clause, the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "it is: that you..."

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «فوربّ السماء والأرض إنه لحق مثل ما أنكم تنطقون» there is the art of the oath (fann al-qasam), which has already been referred to. It is that the speaker wishes to swear about something and swears by that which contains pride for him, or magnification of his standing, or exaltation of his rank, or that which is a censure of another, or runs in the manner of amatory tenderness, or comes in the manner of admonition and asceticism. So He, glory be to Him, swore an oath that necessitates pride, since it contains self-praise through the greatest power and the most exalted majesty.

* Benefits:
Al-Aṣmaʿī related, saying: "I came away from the great mosque of Basra, and a bedouin appeared on a mount of his, and said: 'Who is the man?' I said: 'From Banū Ajmaʿ.' He said: 'From where have you come?' I said: 'From a place where the speech of the All-Merciful is recited.' He said: 'Recite to me.' So I recited «وَالذَّارِيَاتِ»... and when I reached His saying, the Exalted, «وفي السماء رزقكم», he said: 'Enough for you.' Then he went to his she-camel, slaughtered it, and distributed it among all who came and went, then took his sword and bow and broke them, and went off. Later, when I made the pilgrimage with al-Rashīd, I was circumambulating when someone called to me in a thin voice. I turned and there was the bedouin, grown lean and yellow. He greeted me and asked me to recite the sura; when I reached the verse he cried out and said: 'We have found what our Lord promised us to be true.' Then he said: 'Is there anything beyond this?' So I recited: «فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق». He cried out and said: 'Glory be to Allah! Who is it that angered the Majestic so that He swore, and they did not believe Him in His saying until they forced Him to an oath?' He said it three times, and his soul departed with them."

dervis-irab:24-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضَيْفِ) Ḍayf is used for one and for many, because it is originally a maṣdar, like zawr and ṣawm. It was said they were twelve angels. In al-Qāmūs: "Ḍayf is for the singular and the plural; it may also be pluralised as aḍyāf, ḍuyūf and ḍayfān; and she is a ḍayf and a ḍayfa." As for ḍayfan, he is one who comes along with the guest as a sponger. In al-Asās: Ḍāfa ilayhi means "he inclined to him", and ḍāfa ʿanhu "he inclined away from him"; ḍāfa l-sahmu ʿani l-hadaf "the arrow veered from the target"; and "the sun ḍāfat, ḍayyafat and taḍayyafat" means it inclined toward setting. Bishr said:
طاو برملة أورال تضيفه ... إلى الكناس عشيّ بارد صرد
(Gaunt, on the sands of Awrāl, a cold, bitter evening inclined him toward his lair.) That is, it inclined him toward it. "The she-camel tuḍīfu to the stallion and the girl tuḍīfu to the man" means she takes comfort in his voice and wishes to go to him; "aḍif ẓahraka ilā l-ḥāʾiṭ" means "lean your back against the wall". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فلما دخلناه أضفنا ظهورنا ... إلى كل حاري جديد مشطّب
(When we entered it we leaned our backs against every new, striped, sand-hewn wall.) And "they alighted at ḍayf al-wādī" means at its side; "taḍāyafū l-wādī" means they came to its side; "ḍāfanī and taḍayyafanī" (he was my guest). Al-Farazdaq said:
ومنّا خطيب لا يعاب وقائل ... ومن هو يرجو فضله المتضيف
(Among us is an orator who is not faulted, and a speaker, and one whose bounty the guest hopes for.) And "aḍaftuhu and ḍayyaftuhu" (I hosted him), and he is a ḍayf, and likewise the plural; they are ḍuyūf, aḍyāf and ḍayfān.
(فَراغَ) Rāgha means to go off secretly, and this is part of the host's good manners, that he surprise his guest with his hospitality. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Rāgha l-thaʿlabu rawghan (verb pattern qāla) and rawaghānan: it went right and left quickly and deceptively, so it does not settle in one direction; and 'rāgha fulān ilā kadhā' means he inclined to it secretly."
(فَأَوْجَسَ) He concealed within himself.
(صَرَّةٍ) With fatḥa on the ṣād, it is intensity of shouting, wailing and groaning from the heat of fever, and "ṣarra the pen and the door" (they creaked). It was also said: a group of people. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "Al-ṣarra: the uproar and the cry. Al-ṣarra: the group. Al-ṣarra: severity, of war or otherwise."
(فَصَكَّتْ) There is disagreement about ṣakk. It was said to be striking with the open hand; it was also said to be striking the face with the fingertips as one who is astonished, which is the habit of women when they find something strange. The origin of ṣakk is striking one thing with a broad thing.
(خَطْبُكُمْ) Your affair. Khaṭb originally means a grave matter, and from it comes the khuṭba, because it is eloquent speech aimed at grave matters.
(مُسَوَّمَةً) Marked, from sawma, which is the mark.

* I'rab:
(هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْراهِيمَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ) hal is an interrogative particle, and the interrogation here means magnification and alerting that the account was not from the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he knew it only by revelation. أَتاكَ is a verb with a fronted direct object; ضَيْفِ إِبْراهِيمَ is annexed to الْحَدِيثُ; and الْمُكْرَمِينَ is an adjective of ضَيْفِ. (إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقالُوا سَلاماً قالَ سَلامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ) إِذْ is an adverb for time that has passed, accusative either by الْمُكْرَمِينَ because Abraham honoured them, or by the verbal sense contained in ضَيْفِ, or by an implied "اذكر" (remember), or by حَدِيثُ, that is, "has the account of them reached you, at the time of their entering upon him?"; Ibn Hishām preferred this because it is a maṣdar with a whiff of the verb. The clause دَخَلُوا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and عَلَيْهِ is attached to دَخَلُوا; فَقالُوا is conjoined to دَخَلُوا; سَلاماً is an absolute object whose verb was dispensed with because it takes its place, its origin being "we greet you with a greeting"; قالَ is a past verb with a latent agent, implied "he"; سَلامٌ is a mubtadaʾ, and commencing with it was permissible although indefinite because it contains the sense of a supplication; the shift to the nominative by inchoation was to indicate permanence and continuity of the greeting, so that his salutation would be better than theirs; the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "سلام عليكم". Both were read in the nominative. قَوْمٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, implied "وأنتم" or "هم", and مُنْكَرُونَ is an adjective of قَوْمٌ. (فَراغَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ فَجاءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element required by the context, that is, "so he hastened to honour them without letting them notice", since part of the etiquette of hospitality is that the host surprise his guests with food without their noticing him, for fear they would spare him the trouble; hence رَاغَ. رَاغَ is a past verb with a latent agent, and إِلى أَهْلِهِ is attached to رَاغَ; فَجاءَ is a conjunction of immediate sequence; بِعِجْلٍ is attached to جَاءَ and سَمِينٍ is an adjective of عِجْلٍ. (فَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قالَ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded; إِلَيْهِمْ is attached to قَرَّبَهُ; أَلا is a particle of interrogation and lā is negative, the interrogation meaning offering or rebuke; تَأْكُلُونَ is a nominative imperfect verb, and the clause is the content of the saying. (فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element required by the context, that is, "when he saw their abstaining and their insistence on abstaining, he sensed fear of them", thinking they intended to harm him; خِيفَةً is the object of أَوْجَسَ. (قالُوا لا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ) lā is prohibitive, and تَخَفْ is an imperfect verb jussive by lā; بَشَّرُوهُ is a past verb with agent and direct object; بِغُلامٍ is attached to بَشَّرُوهُ, and عَلِيمٍ is an adjective of غُلامٍ. (فَأَقْبَلَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَها وَقالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ) Also conjoined to an implied element that is indispensable, that is, "when Sarah, Abraham's wife, heard the good news, she came forward crying out". امْرَأَتُهُ is the agent of فَأَقْبَلَتِ; فِي صَرَّةٍ is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl, that is, "ṣārra" (crying out); فَصَكَّتْ is conjoined to فَأَقْبَلَتِ; وَجْهَها is a direct object; وَقالَتْ is also conjoined; عَجُوزٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "I am an old woman", and عَقِيمٌ is an adjective, that is, "I am an old woman, barren, so how shall I give birth?" ʿAqīm is of the pattern faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, in which masculine and feminine are alike, that is, "made barren", as though she were bound with a tie; one also says "a man ʿaqīm". He said:
عقم النساء فما يلدن شبيهه ... إن النساء بمثله عقيم
(Women have been made barren and bear none like him; truly, women are barren of his like.) (قالُوا كَذلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ) قالُوا is a verb and agent; كَذلِكَ is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "a saying like that which we said"; قالَ رَبُّكِ is a verb and agent; inna and its noun; هُوَ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or ʿimād, with no position; الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ are two khabars of inna. (قالَ فَما خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ) قالَ is a past verb whose agent is latent, that is, Abraham; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it makes explicit an implied conditional, that is, "if you are angels as you say, then what is your business?"; مَا is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and خَطْبُكُمْ is the khabar; أَيُّهَا is a vocative from which the vocative particle is omitted, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is a specified indefinite, and the hāʾ is for alerting; الْمُرْسَلُونَ is a badal. (قالُوا إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنا إِلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ) inna and its noun; the clause أُرْسِلْنا is the khabar, and nā is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause أُرْسِلْنا is the khabar of inna; inna and what is within its scope is the content of the saying; إِلى قَوْمٍ is attached to أُرْسِلْنا, and مُجْرِمِينَ is an adjective. (لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِنْ طِينٍ) The lām is for justification; نُرْسِلَ is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied an after the lām of justification, the agent being latent, implied "نحن"; عَلَيْهِمْ is attached to نُرْسِلَ; حِجارَةً is a direct object, and مِنْ طِينٍ is an adjective of حِجارَةً; the lām of justification and its genitive noun are attached to أُرْسِلْنا. (مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ) مُسَوَّمَةً is a second adjective of حِجارَةً or a ḥāl from it, since it was described by the preposition and its genitive noun; عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ, the adverbial, is attached to مُسَوَّمَةً, and لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ is also attached to مُسَوَّمَةً. (فَأَخْرَجْنا مَنْ كانَ فِيها مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ)
The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it makes explicit clauses that have been omitted; أَخْرَجْنا is a verb and agent; مَنْ is an object; كانَ is an incomplete past verb whose noun is latent, implied "هم", and فِيها is its khabar; مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is a ḥāl; the clause كانَ is the ṣila of the relative and has no position; and the pronoun in فِيها refers to the towns of the people of Lot, though they were not mentioned, since they were known. (فَما وَجَدْنا فِيها غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and مَا is negative; وَجَدْنا is a verb and agent; غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ is a direct object, and مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ is an adjective; they are Lot and his two daughters, and they were described with faith and submission (islām) because they affirmed with their hearts and acted with their limbs. (وَتَرَكْنا فِيها آيَةً لِلَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ) The wāw is a conjunction; تَرَكْنا is a verb and agent, and فِيها is attached to تَرَكْنا; آيَةً is a direct object; لِلَّذِينَ is an adjective of آيَةً; and the clause يَخافُونَ الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ is the ṣila of the relative.

* Rhetoric:
1- The confirmatory interrogative (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī): in His saying «هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين» is a confirmatory interrogative, to magnify the account and to gather the addressee's attention, as when you begin by telling someone something wondrous and ask him whether he has heard it or not, as though you require him to say "no" and ask you for the account.
2- Omission (al-ḥadhf): in His saying «قوم منكرون» there is omission, and there is disagreement about the implied omitted mubtadaʾ. It was said that what suits the state of Abraham, peace be upon him, is that he did not address them with this, given the lack of friendliness in it, which is not hidden; rather the implied form appears to be "هؤلاء قوم منكرون" (these are strange people), and he said it to himself or to those with him of his followers and servants, such that the guests did not hear it. It was also said that he found them strange because they were not among his acquaintances, or not of the kind of people he knew, or he saw in them a state and appearance different from the state and appearance of people; or that this was a question to them, as if he said "you are strange people, so tell me who you are".
3- Mursal metonymy (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying «قالوا لا تخف وبشّروه بغلام عليم» there is a majāz mursal, for the boy was called "knowing" in view of what his affair would become when he grew up.

dervis-irab:38-42.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِرُكْنِهِ) Rukn is the side one leans on. In al-Qāmūs: "Rakana ilayhi (like naṣara, ʿalima and manaʿa) rukūnan: he inclined and settled; al-rukn, with ḍamma, is the stronger side, the great matter, and that by which one is strengthened, of kingship, troops and so on, and might and protection." The meaning of tawallā bi-ruknihi is: he turned away, swerved aside and deviated, headstrong.
(بِرُكْنِهِ)
[Translator's note: the source repeats this headword and its explanation at this point.] Rukn is the side one leans on. In al-Qāmūs: "Rakana ilayhi (like naṣara, ʿalima and manaʿa) rukūnan: he inclined and settled; al-rukn, with ḍamma, is the stronger side, the great matter, and that by which one is strengthened, of kingship, troops and so on, and might and protection." The meaning of tawallā bi-ruknihi is: he turned away, swerved aside and deviated, headstrong.
(مُلِيمٌ) Mulīm is one who has done what is blameworthy, of stubbornness and obstinacy; malūm is one on whom blame has fallen. In the proverb: "Many a blamer is blameworthy, and many a blamed one has no fault."

* I'rab:
(وَفِي مُوسى إِذْ أَرْسَلْناهُ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and وَفِي مُوسى is conjoined to His saying فِيها with repetition of the preposition, because the item conjoined to is a genitive pronoun; it is attached, in meaning, to تَرَكْنا, and the implied form is "and We left in the story of Moses a sign". It may also be attached to an implied جَعَلْنا indicated by وَتَرَكْنا; al-Zamakhsharī allowed that, saying: "or it is conjoined to «وتركنا فيها آية», in the sense of «and We made in Moses a sign»", like the saying "I fed her straw and cold water". Abū Ḥayyān objected to him, saying: "There is no need to imply وجعلنا, since it is possible that the operator on the genitive phrase is وتركنا." إِذْ is an adverb for time that has passed, attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of آيَةً, that is, "a sign existing at the time of Our sending"; you may also attach it to تَرَكْنا. The clause أَرْسَلْناهُ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ is attached to أَرْسَلْناهُ; بِسُلْطانٍ is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl, that is, "supported", and مُبِينٍ is an adjective of سُلْطانٍ. (فَتَوَلَّى بِرُكْنِهِ وَقالَ ساحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; تَوَلَّى is a past verb whose agent is latent, referring to Pharaoh, and بِرُكْنِهِ is a ḥāl from the pronoun of Pharaoh; قالَ is conjoined to تَوَلَّى; ساحِرٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "he is a sorcerer"; أَوْ is a conjunction of vagueness for the hearer, or of doubt: he put himself in the position of one in doubt although he knew him to be a true prophet, as a deception of his people; مَجْنُونٌ is conjoined to ساحِرٌ. 
[Translator's note: at this point the source runs straight on, without a break, into the next verse, reading "ساحرَأَخَذْناهُ وَجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ)", with the opening of the parenthesis and the fāʾ of «فَأَخَذْناهُ» missing; the verse is reproduced here as it is plainly intended.]
(فَأَخَذْناهُ وَجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; أَخَذْناهُ is a verb, agent and direct object; وَجُنُودَهُ may be conjoined to the object of أَخَذْناهُ, which is preferable, or be an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu); فَنَبَذْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ is conjoined to أَخَذْناهُ, and فِي الْيَمِّ is attached to نَبَذْناهُمْ; وَهُوَ: the wāw is circumstantial, and هُوَ is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ, and مُلِيمٌ is the khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the object of نَبَذْناهُمْ or of أَخَذْناهُ. The difference between the two ḥāls is that the wāw in the first is obligatory, since it contains no mention of a pronoun returning to the owner of the ḥāl, while in the second it is not obligatory, since the clause contains a pronoun returning to it. (وَفِي عادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ) Conjoined to what preceded, and what was said about «وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه» is said about it; عَلَيْهِمُ is attached to أَرْسَلْنا, الرِّيحَ is a direct object, and الْعَقِيمَ is an adjective of الرِّيحَ. (ما تَذَرُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَالرَّمِيمِ) مَا is negative; تَذَرُ is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is latent, implied "هي", that is, the wind, and the clause is a ḥāl from الرِّيحَ; مِنْ is a redundant preposition, and شَيْءٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a direct object; the clause أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ is an adjective of شَيْءٍ; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; جَعَلَتْهُ is a verb, latent agent and direct object, and the clause is in the position of the second object of تَذَرُ, as if it were said "it leaves nothing except as something made"; كَالرَّمِيمِ is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the second object of جَعَلَتْهُ, or the kāf is a noun meaning "like", a direct object, with الرَّمِيمِ as its muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His saying «الريح العقيم» there is an istiʿāra makniyya. He likened what is in the wind of the quality that prevents the production of rain or the pollination of trees to what is in the woman of the quality mentioned that prevents conception; then "barren" (ʿaqīm) was said, and that meaning was intended, by the indication of the wind's being described by it. The one borrowed for is the wind, the one borrowed from is the female able to bear offspring, and the borrowed thing is barrenness, which is the absence of offspring. The common ground between the one borrowed for and the one borrowed from is the absence of offspring. It is a metaphor of a perceived thing for a perceived thing, on the strength of sharing in an intellectual matter, and it is among the most delicate of metaphors.

dervis-irab:43-48.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصَّاعِقَةُ) That which falls from the sky; al-ṣāʿiqa is that which strikes (taṣqaʿu) the heads. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: al-ṣāʿiqa and al-ṣāqiʿa are the same, and he recited:
يحكون بالمصقولة القواطع ... تشقق البرق من الصواقع
(They rub with the polished, cutting [blades], as lightning splits from the thunderbolts.) As for al-ṣaʿqa, it was said to be like the zajra, which is the sound that comes from the thunderbolt. A certain rajaz poet said:
لاح سحاب فرأينا برقه ... ثم تدانى فسمعنا صعقه
(A cloud appeared and we saw its lightning; then it drew near and we heard its crash.) In al-Mukhtār: "Al-ṣāʿiqa is fire that falls from the sky in a violent thunder. One says 'ṣaʿaqathum al-samāʾ' (verb pattern qaṭaʿa) when it hurls the thunderbolt upon them. Al-ṣāʿiqa is also the cry of punishment."

* I'rab:
(وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا حَتَّى حِينٍ) Also conjoined to what preceded. The clause تَمَتَّعُوا is the content of the saying; حَتَّى is a particle of limit and of the genitive, and حِينٍ is genitive by حَتَّى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تَمَتَّعُوا. (فَعَتَوْا عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction of reported sequence; عَتَوْا is a verb and agent, and عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ is attached to عَتَوْا; فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ is conjoined to عَتَوْا; the wāw is circumstantial, هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يَنْظُرُونَ is the khabar, and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (فَمَا اسْتَطاعُوا مِنْ قِيامٍ وَما كانُوا مُنْتَصِرِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and مَا is negative; اسْتَطاعُوا is a verb and agent; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and قِيامٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a direct object; the wāw is a conjunction and مَا negative; كانُوا is an incomplete past verb, the wāw its noun, and مُنْتَصِرِينَ its khabar. (وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and قَوْمَ is accusative by an omitted verb understood implicitly, that is, "and We destroyed the people of Noah"; you may also imply "and remember the people of Noah". It was also read with the genitive, conjoined to «وفي ثمود». As for مِنْ قَبْلُ: مِنْ is a preposition and قَبْلُ an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording and not in meaning; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. inna and its noun, and the clause كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ is its khabar; the clause of inna and what follows it has no position, because it is a justification of their destruction. (وَالسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and السَّماءَ is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation), the implied form being "بنينا السماء بنيناها"; بَنَيْناها is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause has no position because it is explanatory; the clause "بنينا السماء" is conjoined to the preceding verbal clause, and for that reason the accusative is preferred. The generality read it so, and only two read it with the nominative, neither of the Seven, namely Abū l-Sammāl and Ibn Miqsam. بِأَيْدٍ may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the agent of بَنَيْناها, that is, "endowed with strength", or from its object, that is, "endowed with strength"; it may also be attached to بَنَيْناها, in which case the bāʾ is causal, that is, "by reason of Our power". The wāw is circumstantial; inna and its noun, the shifted lām, and مُوسِعُونَ is its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of بَنَيْناها or from its object. The meaning of مُوسِعُونَ is "able", from wusʿ, which is capacity; and al-mūsiʿ is one strong in spending. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Wasiʿa Allāhu ʿalayhi rizqahu yasaʿu (with regular form) wasʿan (verb pattern nafaʿa): He expanded and increased it; awsaʿahu and wassaʿahu, with alif and with tashdīd, are the same; and awsaʿa l-rajulu, with alif, means the man became possessed of ample means and wealth." (وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْناها فَنِعْمَ الْماهِدُونَ) Conjoined to the preceding sentence, and its i'rab proceeds as it did there. فَنِعْمَ: the fāʾ is a conjunction and نِعْمَ is a past verb, fixed (jāmid), for the expression of praise; الْماهِدُونَ is the agent of نِعْمَ, and the one specified for praise is omitted, that is, "نحن" (We), so the sentence is its khabar.

dervis-irab:49-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَفِرُّوا) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Farra min ʿaduwwihi yafirru (verb pattern ḍaraba) firāran: he fled; farra l-fārisu farran: the horseman made wide his circling in order to wheel about; and farra ilā l-shayʾ: he went to it."
(أَتَواصَوْا) Tawāṣī is that people charge one another; the waṣiyya (charge) is mainly in commanding important things together with prohibiting contravention.
(ذَنُوباً) Dhanūb, with fatḥa on the dhāl, is the large bucket. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-dhanūb is the bucket that has a tail (dhanab)", and it is used as feminine and masculine. He said:
لنا ذنوب ولكم ذنوب ... فإن أبيتم فلنا القليب
(We have a bucketful and you have a bucketful; and if you refuse, then the well is ours.) And ʿAlqama said:
وفي كل حيّ قد ضبطت بنعمة ... فحقّ لشاس من نداك ذنوب
(In every tribe you have taken hold with a favour, so it is only right that Shās have a bucketful of your bounty.)

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنا زَوْجَيْنِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ may be attached to خَلَقْنا, that is, "We created two pairs from everything", or to an omitted element, a ḥāl from زَوْجَيْنِ, because it was originally an adjective of it, the implied form being "We created two pairs, existing from everything". خَلَقْنا is a verb and agent, and زَوْجَيْنِ a direct object; laʿalla and its noun, and the clause تَذَكَّرُونَ is its khabar; the origin is تَتَذَكَّرُونَ, one of the two tāʾs having been omitted. (فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, "if you know that Allah the Exalted is One, with no peer or equal, then flee to Him, affirm His oneness, and associate nothing with Him"; an omitted muḍāf must be implied, that is, "to His reward". فِرُّوا is an imperative indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; إِلَى اللَّهِ is attached to فِرُّوا; inna and its noun; لَكُمْ is attached to نَذِيرٌ, and likewise مِنْهُ, or you may attach it to an omitted element as a ḥāl from نَذِيرٌ, because it was originally an adjective of it; نَذِيرٌ is the khabar of inna and مُبِينٌ an adjective of نَذِيرٌ. (وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction, lā prohibitive, and تَجْعَلُوا an imperfect verb jussive by lā, the wāw its agent; مَعَ اللَّهِ is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element in the position of the second object; إِلهاً is the first object of تَجْعَلُوا, and آخَرَ an adjective of إِلهاً. The i'rab of «إني لكم منه نذير مبين» has been given before, and this sentence is a repetition for emphasis: the first is consequent on abandoning faith and obedience, and the second consequent on associating partners with Him. (كَذلِكَ ما أَتَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا قالُوا ساحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ) The kāf is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "the matter and affair"; مَا is negative and أَتَى a past verb; الَّذِينَ is its fronted object, and مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ is attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and رَسُولٍ is genitive by مِنْ in form and nominative in position because it is the agent; the clause has no position because it is explanatory; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; قالُوا is a verb and agent; ساحِرٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "أنت" (you); أَوْ is a conjunction, and مَجْنُونٌ is conjoined to ساحِرٌ, the meaning of the conjunction having been given earlier. The clause إِلَّا قالُوا is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ, as if it were said: "No messenger came to those before them except in a state of their saying 'he is a sorcerer or a madman.'" (أَتَواصَوْا بِهِ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ) The hamza is for rebuking, reproving, expressing wonder (istifhām inkārī tawbīkhī taʿajjubī); تَواصَوْا is a past verb and agent, the wāw being its agent, and بِهِ is attached to تَواصَوْا; بَلْ is a particle of turning away and of conjunction; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ, قَوْمٌ the khabar, and طاغُونَ an adjective of قَوْمٌ. (فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَما أَنْتَ بِمَلُومٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, "if this is their way, and you have tested and experienced it yourself, then turn away from them"; فَتَوَلَّ is an imperative indeclinable on the omission of the weak letter, and the agent is latent, implied "أنت"; عَنْهُمْ is attached to تَوَلَّ; the fāʾ gives the reason for the command; مَا is the Ḥijāzī negative, أَنْتَ is its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and مَلُومٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the khabar of مَا. (وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ذَكِّرْ is an imperative whose agent is latent, implied "أنت"; the fāʾ gives the reason for the command; inna and its noun, and the clause تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is its khabar. (وَما خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنْسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ) The wāw is a conjunction and مَا negative; خَلَقْتُ is a verb and agent; الْجِنَّ is a direct object and الْإِنْسَ is conjoined to الْجِنَّ; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; the lām is for justification or for consequence (lil-ʿāqiba) [Translator's note: the source reads «للعاقة»; «للعاقبة» is evidently intended]; يَعْبُدُونِ is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied an, permissibly, after the lām of justification, the sign of its accusative being the omission of the nūn, and the nūn mentioned is the nūn of protection (wiqāya); the wāw is the agent, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is in the position of the accusative as a direct object; the lām of justification and what follows it are attached to خَلَقْتُ. More discussion of this verse, about which disagreement has branched out, will follow. (ما أُرِيدُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ وَما أُرِيدُ أَنْ يُطْعِمُونِ) مَا is negative; أُرِيدُ is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is latent, implied "أنا"; مِنْهُمْ is attached to أُرِيدُ; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and رِزْقٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the object of أُرِيدُ; the wāw is a conjunction, and وَما أُرِيدُ is conjoined to its like; أَنْ is a particle of maṣdar and of accusative, and يُطْعِمُونِ is an imperfect verb accusative by أَنْ, the omitted yāʾ of the speaker being a direct object; أَنْ and what lies within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, a direct object, that is, "and I do not desire their feeding Me". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ) inna and its noun; هُوَ is a separating pronoun with no position; الرَّزَّاقُ is the first khabar of inna, ذُو الْقُوَّةِ a second khabar, and الْمَتِينُ a third; it was also said to be an adjective of الرَّزَّاقُ or of ذُو. (فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوباً مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحابِهِمْ فَلا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ) The fāʾ
is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, "if you have come to know the state of the disbelievers mentioned above, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of Noah, then these deniers have a share like theirs"; more on this will come in the section on rhetoric. inna is a particle resembling the verb; لِلَّذِينَ is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative, the fronted khabar of inna, and the clause ظَلَمُوا is the ṣila of the relative; ذَنُوباً is the postponed noun of inna, and مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحابِهِمْ is an adjective of ذَنُوباً; the fāʾ is a conjunction for ordering the prohibition of hastening; lā is prohibitive and يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ an imperfect verb jussive by lā, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, the wāw its agent, the nūn mentioned the kasra-vowelled nūn of protection, and the omitted yāʾ a direct object. (فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ يَوْمِهِمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction for ordering the establishment of the "woe", that is, severe punishment, for them; وَيْلٌ is a mubtadaʾ, and commencing with it was permissible because of the sense of supplication it contains; لِلَّذِينَ is its khabar, and the clause كَفَرُوا is the ṣila of the relative; مِنْ يَوْمِهِمُ is an adjective of وَيْلٌ, and al-Jalāl determined that it means "in", which is one of the meanings of مِنْ that the author of al-Mughnī brought to fifteen, and he exemplified it by His saying, the Exalted, «إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة», that is, "on the day of Friday"; الَّذِي is an adjective of يَوْمِهِمُ, and يُوعَدُونَ is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw the nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause يُوعَدُونَ is the ṣila of الَّذِي.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «الجن والإنس» there is ṭibāq (antithesis). The meaning of «إلا ليعبدون» is "except that they be prepared and made ready for worship", for I created in them reason and implanted in them the senses and the ability that enable them to worship. This does not contradict the failure of some of them actually to worship, because this lagging portion, even if it does not worship Allah, has the readiness and preparedness implanted in it, which in truth is the goal. A disagreement has branched out between the Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila about this verse, and the fact is that there is no disagreement, because the verse was brought only to declare His majesty, glory be to Him, and that His relation with His servants cannot be measured by the relation of created masters with their servants: their servants are required to serve and to earn for their masters, and by means of the earnings of their servants the measure of their livelihood is determined, whereas Allah the Exalted asked no provision of His servants nor to be fed, but asks of them only His worship and nothing else; and in addition to His not asking provision of them, it is He who provides for them. There are arguments here for which the scope of this book is too narrow, so they should be sought in their proper places.
2- Representative explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying «فإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم فلا يستعجلون» there is an istiʿāra tamthīliyya taṣrīḥiyya, because the origin lies with the water-givers who divide the water, so this one has a bucketful and that one has a bucketful. He said:
لنا ذنوب ولكم ذنوب ... فإن أبيتم فلنا القليب
(We have a bucketful and you have a bucketful; and if you refuse, then the well is ours.) And when ʿAmr ibn Shās said: [Translator's note: the source reads «عمرو بن شاس» here, whereas the verses that follow are attributed elsewhere in the same entry to ʿAlqama, with Shās/Shaʾs being the name of his brother; the source is translated as written.]
وفي كل حيّ قد خبطت بنعمة ... فحقّ لشأس بعد ذاك ذنوب
(In every tribe you have bestowed a favour, so it is only right that Shaʾs after that have a bucketful.) [Translator's note: this verse differs from the version quoted in the Vocabulary section (ضبطت / لشاس ... من نداك ذنوب); both are given as in the source.] The king said: "Yes, and a great many more."
And the text of al-Mubarrad in al-Kāmil: "The origin of al-dhanūb is the bucket, as I mentioned to you. ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada said to al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Shamir al-Ghassānī (some say Shamir and some say Shammar), whose brother, namely Shaʾs ibn ʿAbada, was held captive by him, having been taken at the battle of ʿAyn Abāgh (some say Ibāgh), in the battle that took place between him and al-Mundhir ibn Māʾ al-Samāʾ, in a poem in which he praised him:
وفي كل حيّ قد خبطت بنعمة ... فحقّ لشأس من نداك ذنوب
(In every tribe you have bestowed a favour, so it is only right that Shaʾs have a bucketful of your bounty.) The king said: Yes, and a great many more."
[Translator's note: the source text ends here, and the opening quotation mark of al-Mubarrad's text is never closed.]

dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الذَّارِياتِ): the winds, because they scatter (tadhrū) dust and other things, i.e. blow them away.
(الحاملات): the clouds, because they carry the rain.
(وِقْراً): with kasra on the wāw, i.e. a load.
(الْحُبُكِ): the rippling that appears on the face of water when the wind strikes it. Al-Buḥturī said, describing the pool of al-Mutawakkil:
إذا علتها الصبا أبدت لها حبكا ... مثل الجواشن مصقولا حواشيها
(When the east wind rises over it, it shows ripples on it like coats of mail, their edges polished.)
And in al-Kashshāf: «Al-ḥubuk are the streaks, like the ripples of water and sand when the wind strikes it; likewise the ḥubuk of hair are the traces of its folding and breaking. Zuhayr said:
مكلل بأصول النجم تنسجه ... ريح خريق لضاحي مائه حبك
(Crowned with the roots of the najm-plant, which a swift cold wind weaves; the exposed surface of its water has ripples.)
And the coat of mail is maḥbūka because its rings are beaten out in streaks.» Zuhayr is describing a sandgrouse that fled from a falcon until it sought refuge from it in a nearby water; and before the verse:
حتى استغاثت بماء لا رشاء له ... من الأباطح في حافاته البرك
(Until it cried for help to a water with no rope, in the broad valleys, with al-burak on its banks.)
and after it:
كما استغاث بسيء فزّ غيطلة ... خاف العيون فلم ينظر به الحشك
(As the fawn of a thicket sought help in its mother's sīʾ-milk, fearing the watchers, and the udder-full one was not looked at.)
He says that this nearby water has no rope, i.e. no cord with which to draw from it, because it has no need of it; "min al-abāṭiḥ" means in wide, level places; "fī ḥāffātihi" means its sides; and al-burak is the plural of burka, a kind of water-bird. It crowns that water with the roots of the najm, i.e. the plant that has no stalk, and "tansijuhu" means bends it in an orderly bending like weaving, so it is an explicit metaphor. Al-kharīq is the cold, and the one fast in going; al-ḍāḥī is the ... [Translator's note: the source prints «الفاهر», apparently a corruption, perhaps for «الظاهر» "the exposed"; I read it so]; al-ḥubuk are the streaks in water when the wind strikes it, the plural of ḥabīka. Al-sayʾ, with fatḥa or kasra, is the milk at the tip of the udder; al-ghazz is the young of the wild cow; al-ghayṭala is the entangled trees, and al-ghazz was annexed to it because it is in it. Al-ʿuyūn here are the watchers of game. Ḥashakat al-durra bi-l-laban ḥashkan wa-ḥushūkan: the udder was full of milk; and in it is an indication that it was thirsty.
(الْخَرَّاصُونَ): the liars. Al-kharṣ is conjecture and guess; one says: "kam kharṣ arḍika?" (with kasra on the khāʾ), "what is the estimate of your land?". The origin of al-kharṣ is cutting, from their saying kharaṣa fulān kalāman wa-ikhtaraṣahu when he cut it off without a basis.
(غَمْرَةٍ): al-ghamra is from ghamarahu al-māʾ yaghmuruhu when it covered him; what is meant here is ignorance.

* I'rab:
(وَالذَّارِياتِ ذَرْواً): The wāw is a particle of oath and of genitive; الذاريات is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; ذروا is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), and the governor in it is the active participle, its object being omitted.
(فَالْحامِلاتِ وِقْراً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; الحاملات is conjoined to الذاريات; وقرا is the direct object of the participle. Whoever read it with fatḥa on the wāw regarded it as a maṣdar, built on naming the thing carried by it.
(فَالْجارِياتِ يُسْراً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; الجاريات is also conjoined to what precedes; يسرا is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl in Sībawayh's view, i.e. "a running possessing ease". It may also be parsed as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar which it has replaced, so it is an absolute object.
(فَالْمُقَسِّماتِ أَمْراً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; المقسمات is also conjoined; أمرا is the direct object of the participle.
(إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ): إن is a particle that resembles a verb; ما is a relative noun, its ism; the clause توعدون is the ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "you are promised it"; the lām is the shifted lām; صادق is the khabar of إن. ما may be a maṣdar, in which case ما and what is within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar which is the ism of إن, i.e. "what you are promised is true"; and the sentence has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath.
(وَإِنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ): conjoined to what precedes.
(وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْحُبُكِ): The wāw is a particle of oath and of genitive; السماء is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; ذات الحبك is an adjective of السماء.
(إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ): إن with its ism; the shifted lām; في قول is attached to an omitted khabar of إن; مختلف is an adjective of قول; and the sentence also has no position, because it is the answer to the oath.
(يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ): The pronoun refers to the Qur'an or to the Messenger, i.e. "he is turned away from it who is turned away", with the turning away than which there is none more severe or greater.
(قُتِلَ الْخَرَّاصُونَ): The sentence is an invocation, with no position; قتل is a passive past verb; الخراصون ... [Translator's note: the source here jumps without a break from the i'rab of «قتل الخراصون» (verse 10) directly to what are evidently words from verse 11 «الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ ساهُونَ», and the printed text reads «والخرّاصون وهم مبتدأ»; the omitted words are not supplied here]. ... and هم is a mubtadaʾ; في غمرة is attached to ساهون; ساهون is their khabar; and the nominal sentence has no position, because it is the ṣila of the relative.
(يَسْئَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ): يسألون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; أيان is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted advanced khabar; يوم الدين is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as the object of يسألون.
(يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ): يوم is an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi) of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "it occurs" or "it comes"; هم is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يفتنون its khabar; على النار is attached to يفتنون, على having the sense of في; and the sentence is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of يوم to it. More on this i'rab will come in the section on benefits.
(ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ): The sentence is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "and it is said to them at the time of punishment: taste". ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; فتنتكم is the direct object; هذا is the mubtadaʾ; الذي is a relative noun, its khabar; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; كان with its ism; به is attached to تستعجلون; and the clause تستعجلون is the khabar of كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy) for the described thing: in His words «يؤفك عنه من أفك» there is a kināya for a described thing, namely the denier who rejects the truth. The pronoun in عنه refers to the Qur'an or to the Messenger, i.e. "he is turned away from it who is turned away, with a turning away than which there is none more severe or greater". It is also said that it refers to the Day of Resurrection. He swore by the scattering winds that the occurrence of the matter of the Resurrection is true; then He swore by the heaven that they are in conflicting speech about its occurrence, some of them doubting and some denying; then He said that he who is the one turned away is turned away from affirming the Day of Resurrection. The benefit of the kināya here is that when He specified this one as the one who is turned away, it conveyed that others are not turned away, as though He said: "turning away is truly established only for this one, and every turning away other than his is counted as non-existent in relation to it".
2- The implied metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in His words «ذوقوا فتنتكم» He likened the punishment to food that is eaten, then omitted the thing likened to and borrowed for it something of its concomitants, namely tasting; its like has already preceded. It is also said that the original meaning of fitna is melting the ore so that its adulteration appears, then it was used for torment and burning. In al-Qāmūs: «al-fatn, with fatḥa, is the kind and the state, and from it "the life is fatnān", i.e. two colours, sweet and bitter; and the burning, and from it «على النار يفتنون».»

* Benefits:
Al-Zajjāj said: «يوم is accusative in two ways. One is that it is on the sense of "the recompense occurs on the day when they are tried over the Fire". The other is that its form is the form of the accusative while its meaning is the meaning of the nominative, because it is annexed to a sentence. You say "يعجبني يوم أنت قائم" and "يوم أنت تقوم": if you wish you put fatḥa, and if you wish you put ḍamma, as the poet said:
لم يمنع الشرب منها غير أن نطقت ... حمامة في غصون ذات أرقال
(Nothing prevented the drinking from it except that a dove cooed in branches that swayed.)
And it is narrated «غير أن نطقت» with ḍamma (on غير), since he annexed غير to أن, which is not firmly established, so he put fatḥa; and likewise when he annexed يوم to the sentence, he put fatḥa.»
